title: Evidence Tagging Taxonomy for RBAC, Audit Logging, and Data Residency
author: Priya Mehta
body:
Summary:
This document defines a unified evidence-tagging taxonomy used across Redwood Inference for RBAC changes, authorization decisions, audit-log events, data residency markers, SDLC gates, and incident response artifacts. The taxonomy standardizes metadata keys, recommended values, retention buckets, storage locations, and ownership to make compliance evidence discoverable and machine-actionable across audits and incident workflows.

Scope:
- Applies to: service-generated audit logs, entitlement change records, model deployment artifacts, CI/CD gate artifacts, incident forensic packages, and cross-region residency markers.
- Excludes: ephemeral debug traces that are intentionally transient and not tagged for long-term retention.

Goals:
1) Ensure all evidence items include a minimum consistent tag set so they can be correlated across systems.
2) Map tags to retention and storage SLA so evidence for regulated customers is preserved according to jurisdictional rules.
3) Provide sample queries and ingestion rules for the audit store and evidence orchestration pipeline.

Minimum tagset (required for all evidence artifacts):
- evidence.id: unique UUID (evidence-123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000)
- evidence.type: one of [rbac_change, authz_decision, audit_event, sdlc_gate, incident_artifact, residency_marker]
- evidence.source: system that emitted the event (e.g., identity-service, policy-engine, runtime-proxy, cicd-pipeline, forensic-collector)
- evidence.actor: principal that initiated action (user:<email> / service:<svc-name> / system)
- evidence.region: region code(s) or region-tag (us-west-2, eu-west-1, GLOBAL)
- evidence.sensitivity: one of [public, internal, restricted, regulated]
- evidence.retention_bucket: one of [30d, 90d, 1y, 3y, 7y, indefinite]
- evidence.owner: team or person responsible for evidence (security, eng-sre, privacy, legal)
- evidence.timestamp: ISO8601 UTC

Example JSON header to attach to artifacts:
{
  "evidence.id": "evidence-123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000",
  "evidence.type": "rbac_change",
  "evidence.source": "identity-service",
  "evidence.actor": "user:alice@redwood.ai",
  "evidence.region": "eu-west-1",
  "evidence.sensitivity": "regulated",
  "evidence.retention_bucket": "7y",
  "evidence.owner": "security",
  "evidence.timestamp": "2025-02-15T14:32:06Z"
}

Tag-to-retention mapping (recommended):
| Tag value category | Typical use cases | Retention bucket | Storage location / notes | Owner |
|--------------------|-------------------|------------------|--------------------------|-------|
| rbac_change | Role grants/revocations, policy updates | 7y | Immutable audit store S3: s3://redwood-audit/immutable/ | security |
| authz_decision | Per-request allow/deny records for regulated customers | 1y (default), 7y if regulated | ElasticSearch + cold S3 tier | eng-sre / security |
| audit_event | Service-level events (deploys, schema changes) | 1y | central audit index | owning-service |
| sdlc_gate | CI approvals, signed SBOMs, dependency-scan reports | 3y | artifacts-bucket + signed manifest | eng-platform / security |
| incident_artifact | Forensic captures, packet captures, preserved logs | indefinite or legal-driven | Forensics vault (restricted access) | security / legal |
| residency_marker | Data residency assertions, geo-tags | per-jurisdiction (see policy) | region-locked storage | privacy/legal |

Note: The table above is a guideline; evidence.sensitivity and contractual/regulatory requirements may increase retention beyond the mapping.

Ingestion and indexing rules (pipeline):
1. All events posted to the centralized ingestion endpoint (/api/v1/evidence/ingest) must include the minimum tagset. Missing required tags result in rejection with HTTP 400 and an export to the onboarding queue.
2. Ingested items are immediately written to a write-ahead object store (encrypted S3) and then indexed into the audit index with tags mapped to searchable fields.
3. If evidence.sensitivity=="regulated", the pipeline will:
   a. Enforce region write (e.g., write to eu-west-1 only).
   b. Apply an "immutable-lock" lifecycle on the object for the specified retention_bucket.
   c. Emit a compliance-notification to the evidence-orchestration bus (Kafka topic: evidence.notifications).

Search and correlation examples (audit index queries):
- Find RBAC changes in a month for a specific user (Elasticsearch DSL):
  {
    "query": {"bool":{"must":[{"term":{"evidence.type":"rbac_change"}},{"term":{"evidence.actor":"user:alice@redwood.ai"}},{"range":{"evidence.timestamp":{"gte":"2025-01-01","lt":"2025-02-01"}}}]}}
  }

Responsibility matrix:
- security: owns taxonomy, compliance rules, forensics vault access, periodic evidence audits.
- eng-sre: owns ingestion pipeline, index availability, and backup integrity.
- eng-platform: ensures SDLC artifacts are tagged at CI gate and signed.
- privacy/legal: approves retention buckets for regulated jurisdictions and retains ability to request extended holds.

Incident response handoff (high-level procedure):
1. Incident commander raises a forensic evidence request ticket (Internal ticket template: EVID-FOR-<INCIDENT-ID>).
2. Forensic collector runs the evidence-export tool with --attach-tags flag which ensures the minimum tagset is embedded and returns an evidence.id.
3. Evidence stored in the forensics vault is assigned evidence.owner=security and evidence.retention_bucket=indefinite (or as requested by legal).
4. Security notifies privacy/legal and triggers preservation hold across any related S3 objects.

Rollout plan and verification checklist (90 days):
- Week 0–2: Publish taxonomy (this doc) and update ingestion API contract.
- Week 3–6: SDK updates and CI gate instrumentation (eng-platform).
- Week 7–10: Pipeline enforcement and test ingestion (eng-sre + security).
- Week 11–12: Pilot with two regulated customers and run evidence retrieval exercises with legal.
- Week 13: Full enforcement and internal audit.

Verification checklist (minimum):
- [ ] All ingestion endpoints validate presence of required tags.
- [ ] Samples from each service contain evidence.owner and evidence.sensitivity set.
- [ ] Immutable-locks are applied for regulated evidence.
- [ ] Evidence retrieval exercise completed within SLA (search-to-restore < 4 hours).

Operational SLOs related to evidence lifecycle:
- Evidence ingestion availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Indexing latency: median < 60s, p95 < 300s.
- Evidence retrieval (cold restore from immutable store): SLA 4 hours for regulated artifacts.

Common anti-patterns and mitigations:
- Missing actor information: fail ingestion and route to developer onboarding.
- Free-text residency markers: replace with canonical evidence.region values enforced by schema.
- Long-lived local copies: disallow local retention of restricted/regulatory artifacts; require uploads to central vault.

Appendix A — Tag glossary (short):
- evidence.id: canonical identifier for cross-system correlation.
- evidence.type: class of artifact used for coarse filtering.
- evidence.source: emitter service or tool name.
- evidence.actor: initiator of event.
- evidence.region: jurisdictional tag.
- evidence.sensitivity: classification used to determine access control and retention.

Appendix B — Quick commands:
- Ingest example (curl):
  curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"evidence.type":"authz_decision","evidence.actor":"service:proxy","evidence.source":"runtime-proxy","evidence.region":"us-west-2","evidence.sensitivity":"internal","evidence.retention_bucket":"1y"}' \
    https://ingest.redwood.internal/api/v1/evidence/ingest
